matches.note: R3 identifies the same non-transactional balance-check/debit race, the missing lock, and the uncalled SERIALIZABLE debitForCashOut, with the same overdraw consequence.
R1 states the exact double-fee defect (debit requested+fee, refund requested−fee); R2 describes the other symptom of the same extra fee debit (wallet driven negative).
R4 covers the fixed refund-"+paymentIntentId key replaying/blocking later cash-outs including the pack-refund collision; R5 covers the missing refundable-amount check on lastPaymentIntentId.

R6 states the same mechanism (all StripeExceptions including timeouts mapped to PaymentGatewayException, catch writes CASH_OUT_REVERSAL) and the same consequence (parent gets both card refund and restored credit); only the reversal-write atomicity detail is omitted.
No reported finding mentions the frontend reading err.response.data.message versus the backend ErrorDto fields; R9 concerns the success toast, not error display.
No reported finding addresses commission/Stripe-fee estimation from gross × live rates, inclusion of credit/pack/refunded bookings, or missing pack-sale revenue.
R8 states that sumTotalCashOuts counts every CASH_OUT_DEBIT and ignores CASH_OUT_REVERSAL rows, inflating the admin overview with cash-outs that never paid out.
Nothing reported touches getCoachRevenueSummary or the estimated Stripe fee subtracted from the coach's net payout.

unmatched_reported.note: Concrete trigger: debits auto-commit before paymentGateway.refund, so a crash or any non-PaymentGatewayException thrown by refund leaves the wallet debited with no refund and no reversal, and no pending state exists to recover from; this failure window is distinct from F1's race and F4's reversal-on-ambiguous-failure.

Toast showing the requested gross instead of net is a UX presentation nit; once the double-fee defect (F2/R1) is fixed the amounts are legitimately gross vs net, and the overdraw remark duplicates R2.

Speculative cent-rounding edge case: Postgres numeric and toCents both round half-up so the claimed ledger/Stripe disagreement is not established by the reported text, and the finding itself hinges on an unverified deserialization assumption.
